title: CLAUDE.md – cfbfastR Development Guide
text: cfbfastR R package provides clean, tidy college football play--play, schedule, roster, ratings, box-score data. wraps CollegeFootballData API (CFBD) ESPN College Football endpoints, exporting 150+ functions across four function-family prefixes: cfbd_*(), espn_cfb_*(), espn_metrics_*(), espn_ratings_*(). Full-season parquet/RDS releases land load_cfb_*(). guide differs current repository docs, treat CONTRIBUTING.md current test implementations authoritative. Version: 2.3.0 (dev) R Requirement: >= 4.1.0 (uses native pipe |>) License: MIT pkgdown site: https://cfbfastr.sportsdataverse.org/ Maintainer: Saiem Gilani (saiem.gilani@gmail.com) Branch: main default branch release branch.

text: CFBD API requires bearer token. Set CFBD_API_KEY environment variable; users can register one via register_cfbd() confirm cfbd_api_key_info() / has_cfbd_key().

title: CLAUDE.md – cfbfastR Development Guide
text: cfbfastR targets R >= 4.1.0 uses native pipe |> exclusively. legacy %>% swept R/, tests/, vignettes/, magrittr longer Imports. New code must use |>. Two patterns don’t port cleanly |>: |>[[("name") – native pipe rejects [[ RHS R 4.1. Use |> purrr::pluck("name") (assign chain temp subset). |> tibble::tibble(col = .data$.) – magrittr quirk created duplicate column. Use tibble::tibble(col = <lhs>) directly.

title: CLAUDE.md – cfbfastR Development Guide
text: Every wrapper returns variable assigned inside tryCatch must initialize variable tryCatch block. Otherwise, API errors (500s, timeouts, HTTP/2 stream errors, connection resets, CFBD rate limits) error handler runs, return variable never bound, return(<var>) throws object '<var>' found instead intended cli::cli_alert_danger() + empty fallback. rule applies every return variable name, just plays_df: df_list, pbp, standings, teams, recruits, coaches, ratings, etc. Initialize appropriate empty value – list() named-list returns, NULL single-object returns, data.frame() tibble returns.
code: cfbd_func <- function(year, ...) {   base_url <- "https://api.collegefootballdata.com/games"   params   <- list(year = year, ...)    plays_df <- data.frame()   # <-- MANDATORY. Not inside tryCatch.    tryCatch(     expr = {       resp <- .cfbd_request(url = base_url, query = params)       plays_df <- resp |>         data.frame(stringsAsFactors = FALSE) |>         dplyr::as_tibble() |>         janitor::clean_names() |>         make_cfbfastR_data("CFBD games from collegefootballdata.com", Sys.time())     },     error = function(e) {       cli::cli_alert_danger(         "{Sys.time()}: Invalid arguments or no data for {.val {year}} available!"       )       cli::cli_alert_danger("Error:\n{conditionMessage(e)}")     },     warning = function(w) {       cli::cli_alert_warning("{Sys.time()}: Warning:\n{conditionMessage(w)}")     },     finally = {}   )   return(plays_df) }

title: CLAUDE.md – cfbfastR Development Guide
text: user-facing messages use cli: cli::cli_alert_danger() errors inside tryCatch handlers cli::cli_alert_warning() warnings inside handlers cli::cli_alert_info() / cli::cli_alert_success() progress success cli::cli_warn() / cli::cli_abort() raised conditions (e.g., argument validation, mis-set API key) pass raw condition objects cli_* calls – glue-interpolated unparenthesized {e} try coerce condition character. Always extract message first value placeholder:
code: # WRONG -- glue tries to interpolate the condition itself cli::cli_alert_danger("Error: {e}")  # RIGHT -- pass the message string cli::cli_alert_danger("Error: {conditionMessage(e)}")

text: CFBD ESPN add columns time without removing old ones, occasionally rename drop columns. Two guardrails apply: Inside functions – dropping known-transient column, use dplyr::select(-dplyr::any_of("colname")) instead dplyr::select(-"colname"). bare form errors moment upstream drops column; any_of() -ops silently. text: Function default arguments must single chosen value, c(...) vector. Document allowed choices @param validate inside body cli::cli_abort(). rely match.arg(c(...)) – conflates “default” “allowed set”, caller passing value front vector silently gets first element. : : pattern enforced across catalog v2 PBP entry points.
code: cfbd_pbp_data_v2 <- function(year, week = NULL,                              output = c("default", "lean", "full"), ...) {   output <- match.arg(output)   # ... } #' @param output Column tier to return. One of `"default"` (recommended baseline), #'   `"lean"` (compact dashboard set), or `"full"` (every modeled column). cfbd_pbp_data_v2 <- function(year, week = NULL,                              output = "default", ...) {   if (!is.character(output) || length(output) != 1L ||       !output %in% c("default", "lean", "full")) {     cli::cli_abort(c(       "{.arg output} must be one of {.val default}, {.val lean}, or {.val full}.",       "i" = "Got {.val {output}}."     ))   }   # ... }

title: CLAUDE.md – cfbfastR Development Guide
text: get_req() (R/utils.R) resolves outbound proxy three tiers: Explicit proxy = argument (caller-supplied; highest precedence). getOption("cfbfastR.proxy") – session-level fallback. Set options(cfbfastR.proxy = ...) every call flows get_req() picks . http_proxy / https_proxy / no_proxy environment variables – libcurl reads automatically explicit proxy supplied. proxy value (whether passed via argument option) accepts either form: URL string – "http://host:port", forwarded httr2::req_proxy(url = ...). named list – list(url = "...", port = 8080, username = "...", password = "...", auth = "basic"), spread keyword args httr2::req_proxy() authenticated proxies. Per-call override works wrappers thread ... get_req() – typically cfbd_*() family. Wrappers call get_req() without proxy argument (ESPN catalog) rely option / env-var path. adding new wrapper, prefer threading proxy = NULL (...) get_req() callers can override per-call without resetting session option. ESPN catalog wrappers use httr2 hood, env-var path Just Works even without explicit proxy argument.

title: CLAUDE.md – cfbfastR Development Guide
text: play--play / EPA / WPA stack lives R/pbp_*.R. 2.3.0 two side--side surfaces: Legacy entry points: cfbd_pbp_data() (CFBD source) original espn_cfb_pbp() (ESPN source). remain exported behavior-preserved downstream consumers. v2 entry points: cfbd_pbp_data_v2() espn_cfb_pbp_v2(). Thin orchestrators shared .run_epa_wpa() engine. modular pipeline: Adapters (pbp_adapters.R) – .espn_to_epa_input() .cfbd_to_epa_input() translate raw ESPN / CFBD payloads canonical input frame engine understands. Engine (pbp_epa_wpa_engine.R) – .run_epa_wpa() consumes canonical frame, calls create_epa() + create_wpa_naive(), returns frame whose play taxonomy governed .pbp_play_types() (pbp_play_types.R) whose column order governed .pbp_output_order (pbp_output_schema.R). Output tiers – output = "default" (recommended baseline), output = "lean" (compact dashboard subset), output = "full" (every modeled column, including intermediate diagnostics). tier enforced scalar-default + cli::cli_abort validation pattern verified tier-monotonicity tests (lean ⊆ default ⊆ full). Game-meta bridge – ESPN, .espn_pbp_game_meta() resolves team / venue / coach metadata bare PBP payload omits. ESPN returns $ref placeholder instead inlined team record, .espn_pbp_game_meta() falls back .espn_cfb_team_lookup() resulting row still full team metadata. See “Common Pitfalls” . equivalence harness tests/testthat/test-pbp_equivalence.R asserts cfbd_pbp_data_v2() espn_cfb_pbp_v2() reproduce legacy outputs column--column, explicit allow-list intentional representation deltas (character id_play, logical scoring_play, total clock_seconds, v2 short-name passer_player_name / rusher_player_name / receiver_player_name).

Use schema-affecting upstream changes debugging stale-payload issues. cache per-session memory backend persistent filesystem backend (stored tools::R_user_dir("cfbfastR", "cache")). title: CLAUDE.md – cfbfastR Development Guide
text: Always use subset direction column assertions. APIs add columns, strict expect_equal break new column. rule : expected list must subset actual columns. Anti-patterns avoid: dynamic columns, expect_true((core_cols %% colnames(x))) equivalent subset-direction expect_in().
code: test_that("CFBD games endpoint returns expected columns", {   skip_on_cran()   skip_on_ci()   skip_cfbd_test()  # Requires CFBD_API_KEY env var    x <- cfbd_games(year = 2023, week = 1)    # Skip-if-empty guard -- always right after the API call, before any assertion   # that touches x. Handles transient 500s and CFBD rate-limit hiccups.   if (is.null(x) || !is.data.frame(x) || nrow(x) == 0) {     skip("No rows returned from endpoint at test time")   }    cols_x <- c("id", "season", "week", "home_team", "away_team")   expect_in(sort(cols_x), sort(colnames(x)))   # expected ⊆ actual   expect_s3_class(x, "data.frame") }) # WRONG - flags when upstream adds a column, even though it's non-breaking expect_equal(sort(colnames(x)), sort(cols_x))  # WRONG - same direction problem, just phrased with expect_in expect_in(sort(colnames(x)), sort(cols_x))

title: CLAUDE.md – cfbfastR Development Guide
text: Game length: four 15-minute quarters, 60 minutes regulation. v2 PBP clock_seconds column total seconds remaining (start game = 3600), period-relative. Overtime: untimed, alternating possessions 25-yard line. engine models OT possessions drives period >= 5. Season convention: “season” calendar year fall season (e.g., 2023 Rose Bowl played January 2024 season = 2023). CFBD season_type: one "regular", "postseason", "". Cache keys include season_type. CFBD bearer token: CFBD_API_KEY env var. Register https://collegefootballdata.com/key set via register_cfbd(). CFBD rate limits: free-tier callers hit per-minute cap quickly. Catch 429 back ; retry hot.

text: Live-API tests follow subset direction rule column assertions: expected list must subset actual columns, upstream-added column never breaks test. Anti-patterns avoid: dynamic columns, expect_true((core_cols %% colnames(x))) equivalent.
code: test_that("CFBD endpoint returns expected columns", {   skip_on_cran()   skip_on_ci()   skip_if(Sys.getenv("CFBD_API_KEY") == "", "CFBD_API_KEY not set")    x <- cfbd_games(year = 2023, week = 1)    # Skip-if-empty guard - always right after the API call, before any   # assertion that touches the response. Handles transient 500s.   if (is.null(x) || !is.data.frame(x) || nrow(x) == 0) {     skip("No rows returned from endpoint at test time")   }    expected_cols <- c("game_id", "season", "week", "home_team", "away_team")   expect_in(sort(expected_cols), sort(colnames(x)))   # expected subset-of actual   expect_s3_class(x, "data.frame") }) # WRONG - flags when upstream adds a column, even though it is non-breaking expect_equal(sort(colnames(x)), sort(expected_cols))  # WRONG - same direction problem, just phrased as expect_in() expect_in(sort(colnames(x)), sort(expected_cols))

  if (!valid)   {     x_side <- wp_data$s[r] >= 1800     if (x_side)     {       x_spots <- c(seq_fix(wp_data$s[r] - 400, x_lab_max, -200),                    seq_fix(wp_data$s[r] + 400, x_lab_min, 200))     } else {       x_spots <- c(seq_fix(wp_data$s[r] + 400, x_lab_min, 200),                    seq_fix(wp_data$s[r] - 400, x_lab_max, -200))     }     for (i in 1:length(x_spots))     {       valid <- TRUE       if (nrow(wp_data |>                filter(wp_data$wp[r] - 0.1 < wp & wp < wp_data$wp[r] + 0.1 &                       x_spots[i] - 300 < s & s < x_spots[i] + 300)) > 0)       {         # too close to the WP line         valid <- FALSE       }       if (nrow(wp_data |>                filter(wp_data$wp[r] - 0.1 < y_text & y_text < wp_data$wp[r] + 0.1 &                       x_spots[i] - 600 < x_text & x_text < x_spots[i] + 600)) > 0)       {         # too close to another label         valid <- FALSE       }       if (valid)       {         # we found a spot for it, stop loop         wp_data$x_text[r] <- x_spots[i]         wp_data$y_text[r] <- wp_data$wp[r]         break       }     }   }   # warn about the labels not placed   if (!valid)   {     warning(glue(paste("No room for ({wp_data$s[r]},{round(wp_data$wp[r], 3)}):",                        "{gsub('
',' ',wp_data$text[r])}")))   } } # add on WP boundaries first_row <- data.frame(play_id = 0, qtr = 1, time = "15:00", s = 3600,                         wp = 0.5, wpa = NA, text = as.character(""),                         x_text = 3600, y_text = 0.5, away_score = 0, home_score = 0,                         stringsAsFactors = FALSE) last_row <- data.frame(play_id = 999999, qtr = max(wp_data$qtr), s = x_max - 1,                        time = ifelse(max(wp_data$qtr) >= 5, "FINAL
OT", "FINAL"),                        wp = ifelse(game$result < 0, 1, ifelse(game$result > 0, 0, 0.5)),                        wpa = NA, text = as.character(""), x_text = x_max, y_text = 0.5,                        away_score = game$away_score, home_score = game$home_score,                        stringsAsFactors = FALSE) wp_data <- wp_data |>   filter(posteam != "",          wpa != 0) |>   bind_rows(first_row) |>   bind_rows(last_row) |>   arrange(play_id)

title: Making Animated Win Probability Charts with cfbfastR
text: Now ’re ready plotting. draw_frame() function draw win probability plot given number seconds remaining game. can make changes plot like. Let’s test function make sure plot looks like want running function 6 minutes left game.  Looks great, next create draw_game() function draw every frame GIF.
code:
draw_frame <- function(n_sec) {    # frame data   frm_data <- wp_data |>     filter(s >= n_sec)    # output quarter changes   if (nrow(frm_data |> filter(qtr == max(qtr))) == 1)   {     print(glue("Plotting pbp in quarter {max(frm_data$qtr)}"))   }    # plot   frm_plot <- frm_data |>     ggplot(aes(x = s, y = wp)) +     theme_minimal() +     geom_vline(xintercept = c(3600, x_max), color = "#5555AA") +     geom_segment(x = -3600, xend = -x_max, y = 0.5, yend = 0.5, size = 0.75) +     geom_image(x = x_score, y = 0.82, image = game$away_logo, size = 0.08, asp = 1.5) +     geom_image(x = x_score, y = 0.18, image = game$home_logo, size = 0.08, asp = 1.5) +     geom_line(aes(color = ..y.. < .5), size = 1) +     scale_color_manual(values = c(game$away_color, game$home_color)) +     scale_x_continuous(trans = "reverse",                        minor_breaks = NULL,                        labels = c("KICK
OFF", "END
Q1", "HALF
TIME", "END
Q3", "FINAL"),                        breaks = seq(3600, 0, -900),                        limits = c(3700, x_max - 490)) +     scale_y_continuous(labels = c(glue("{game$home_abr} 100%"),                                   glue("{game$home_abr} 75%"),                                   "50%",                                   glue("{game$away_abr} 75%"),                                   glue("{game$away_abr} 100%")),                        breaks = c(0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 1),                        limits = c(0, 1)) +     coord_cartesian(clip = "off") +     xlab("") +     ylab("") +     labs(title = glue("Win Probability Chart: {game$season} Week {game$wk} {game$away_team} @ {game$home_team}"),          caption = "Data from cfbfastR, Visualization by @LeeSharpeNFL, Adapted for CFB by @JaredDLee") +     theme(legend.position = "none")    # score display   away_score <- max(frm_data$away_score)   home_score <- max(frm_data$home_score)    # clock display   qtr <- case_when(     max(frm_data$qtr) == 1 ~ "1st",     max(frm_data$qtr) == 2 ~ "2nd",     max(frm_data$qtr) == 3 ~ "3rd",     max(frm_data$qtr) == 4 ~ "4th",     max(frm_data$qtr) == 5 ~ "OT",     TRUE ~ as.character(max(frm_data$qtr))   )   clock <- tail(frm_data$time, 1)   clock <- ifelse(substr(clock, 1, 1) == "0", substr(clock, 2, 100), clock)   clock <- paste0(qtr, "
", clock)   clock <- ifelse(grepl("FINAL", tail(frm_data$time, 1)), tail(frm_data$time, 1), clock)    # add score and clock to plot   frm_plot <- frm_plot +     annotate("text", x = -1*x_score, y = 0.71, label = away_score, color = game$away_color, size = 8) +     annotate("text", x = -1*x_score, y = 0.29, label = home_score, color = game$home_color, size = 8) +     annotate("text", x = -1*x_score, y = 0.50, label = clock, color = "#000000", size = 6)    # label key moments   frm_labels <- frm_data |>     filter(text != "")   frm_plot <- frm_plot +     geom_point(frm_labels, mapping = aes(x = s, y = wp),                color = "#000000", size = 2, show.legend = FALSE) +     geom_segment(frm_labels, mapping = aes(x = x_text, xend = s, y = y_text, yend = wp),                  linetype = "dashed", color = "#000000", na.rm=TRUE) +     geom_label(frm_labels, mapping = aes(x = x_text, y = y_text, label = text),                size = 3, color = "#000000", na.rm = TRUE, alpha = 0.8)    # plot the frame   plot(frm_plot, width = 12.5, height = 6.47, dpi = 500) } draw_frame(360) draw_game <- function() {   lapply(wp_data$s, function(n_sec)   {     draw_frame(n_sec)   })   print("Plotting frames for pause")   replicate(40, draw_frame(min(wp_data$s)))   print("Assembling plots into a GIF") }

what: A note on the function names
title: ESPN College Football Cookbook
text: first recipe, one idea worth planting early, pays every recipe . ESPN layer cfbfastR named strict, predictable pattern: <entity> thing asking – team, game, player. <detail> slice thing want – schedule, record, roster. plural form (espn_cfb_teams()) catalog every entity; singular form (espn_cfb_team()) one entity depth. practical upshot: know one function, can guess siblings. espn_cfb_game_teams() gives two teams game, espn_cfb_game_team_roster() almost certainly gives roster team game – . rarely need look anything . just need know want spell way package spells . use four anchor IDs throughout: game 401628339, team 61 (Georgia Tech), athlete 4427191, season 2024.
code: espn_cfb_<entity>_<detail>

what: Recipe 1 – A team’s season at a glance
title: ESPN College Football Cookbook
text: question: want quick scouting snapshot one program – , season went. Start catalog. espn_cfb_teams() (plural – catalog) lookup table whole sport: one row per team, -important team_id feed everything else. Now zoom . espn_cfb_team() (singular – one entity, depth) takes team_id season returns team’s detail record, including home venue. entity. Now want detail – schedule. name writes : espn_cfb_team_schedule(). won/lost summary schedule – another detail entity, another espn_cfb_team_*() function: espn_cfb_team_record(). Notice rhythm recipe. never left espn_cfb_team* shelf: catalog (teams), entity (team), two details entity (team_schedule, team_record). shelf – team_roster(), team_stats(), team_coaches(), team_leaders(), team_events() – can now reach without checking docs first.
code: teams <- espn_cfb_teams() teams |>   filter(team_id == "61") |>   select(team_id, display_name, abbreviation, location, color) gt_team <- espn_cfb_team(team_id = 61, year = 2024) gt_team |>   select(team_id, display_name, venue_name, venue_city, venue_state) gt_sched <- espn_cfb_team_schedule(team_id = 61, year = 2024) gt_sched |>   select(any_of(c("game_id", "week", "game_date",                   "home_team", "away_team"))) |>   head(6) espn_cfb_team_record(team_id = 61, year = 2024) |>   select(any_of(c("team_id", "type", "summary", "wins", "losses")))

what: Recipe 2 – Building a game box score
title: ESPN College Football Cookbook
text: question: Give box score single game – team totals individual player lines. switching entities, team game, prefix switches us: espn_cfb_team_*() becomes espn_cfb_game_*(). grammar, new shelf. First, played, score? espn_cfb_game_teams() two-team summary game. takes format argument – "long" gives one row per team (tidy plotting), "wide" gives one row whole game home_* / away_* columns (handy box-score header). Now team statistical totals. want detail (statistics) team within game – read right left name falls : espn_cfb_game_team_statistics(). Finally individual lines – player box score. <entity> still game, <detail> player_box: Three functions, one game, one consistent prefix. later want per-team leaders, already know espn_cfb_game_team_leaders(); want team’s roster appeared game, espn_cfb_game_team_roster(). guessing names correctly now names really guessed – spelled.
code: game_hdr <- espn_cfb_game_teams(game_id = 401628339, format = "wide") game_hdr |>   select(any_of(c("game_id", "home_team", "home_team_score",                   "away_team", "away_team_score"))) team_stats <- espn_cfb_game_team_statistics(game_id = 401628339) team_stats |>   select(any_of(c("team_id", "team", "stat_name",                   "display_value"))) |>   head(10) player_box <- espn_cfb_game_player_box(game_id = 401628339) player_box |>   select(any_of(c("team", "athlete_display_name", "category",                   "stat_name", "stat_value"))) |>   head(10)

what: Recipe 3 – Play-by-play and who was on the field
title: ESPN College Football Cookbook
text: question: Walk game play play – tell players involved play. espn_cfb_game_pbp() play--play detail game: one tidy row per play. clean play log. interesting part participants argument, decides whether people involved play come along ride. participants = "none" (default) – just plays. participants = "wide" – involved athletes spread columns play row (participant_1_*, participant_2_*, …). Best want one flat table. participants = "long" – one extra row per athlete per play. default wrappers also enrich every team-id column readable team detail – team_detail = TRUE argument see espn_cfb_game_*() functions. turns bare team_id team, team_abbreviation, team colors without manual join. ever want raw, un-joined frame – smaller object, join – pass team_detail = FALSE.
code: pbp <- espn_cfb_game_pbp(game_id = 401628339, participants = "wide") pbp |>   select(any_of(c("play_id", "period_number", "type_text",                   "text"))) |>   head(8) # The participant_* columns ride alongside each play in "wide" mode. pbp |>   select(any_of(grep("participant", names(pbp), value = TRUE))) |>   head(5) # team_detail = TRUE is the default; this just makes it explicit. pbp_plain <- espn_cfb_game_pbp(game_id = 401628339, team_detail = FALSE) ncol(pbp) - ncol(pbp_plain)  # the team-detail columns that the join adds

title: ESPN College Football Cookbook

title: cfbfastR Copilot Instructions
text: Every wrapper returns variable assigned inside tryCatch must initialize variable tryCatch block. Otherwise, API errors (CFBD rate limits, ESPN 500s, HTTP/2 stream errors, connection resets) error handler runs, return variable never bound, return(<var>) throws object '<var>' found instead intended cli::cli_alert_danger() + empty fallback. rule applies every return variable name, just df_list: plays_df, pbp, standings, teams, recruits, coaches, ratings, etc. Initialize appropriate empty value – list() named-list returns, NULL single-object returns, data.frame() tibble returns.
code: cfbd_func <- function(year, ...) {   base_url <- "https://api.collegefootballdata.com/games"   params   <- list(year = year, ...)    df_list <- list()   # <-- MANDATORY. Initialize before tryCatch.    tryCatch(     expr = {       resp    <- .cfbd_request(url = base_url, query = params)       df_list <- resp |>         data.frame(stringsAsFactors = FALSE) |>         dplyr::as_tibble() |>         janitor::clean_names() |>         make_cfbfastR_data("CFBD games", Sys.time())     },     error = function(e) {       cli::cli_alert_danger("{Sys.time()}: No data for {.val {year}}!")       cli::cli_alert_danger("Error: {conditionMessage(e)}")     },     warning = function(w) {       cli::cli_alert_warning("{Sys.time()}: {conditionMessage(w)}")     },     finally = {}   )   return(df_list) }

Always extract message first:
code: # WRONG -- glue tries to interpolate the condition itself cli::cli_alert_danger("Error: {e}")  # RIGHT -- pass the message string cli::cli_alert_danger("Error: {conditionMessage(e)}")

Otherwise, API errors, return(X) throws object 'X' found instead intended empty-frame fallback. CFBD rate limits: free-tier callers hit per-minute cap quickly. wrappers surface cli::cli_alert_danger() 429, retry hot loop – add Sys.sleep() re-run failing range. ESPN $ref payloads: ESPN’s “core” API often returns {"$ref": "https://..."} placeholders instead inlined team / athlete / venue metadata. Route new ESPN wrappers consume team metadata .espn_pbp_game_meta() (falls back .espn_cfb_team_lookup()) rather reading team fields directly. output = c(...) default: declare output = c("default", "lean", "full") call match.arg(). Use single-value default (output = "default") validate cli::cli_abort(). c-vector form silently picks first element caller passes vector. Native pipe + magrittr placeholder: |> support . placeholder. Use _ (R 4.2+) wrap explicit lambda \(x) .... Mixing . |> silently -op. %||% rlang-imported: redefine locally; import via @importFrom rlang %||%. make_cfbfastR_data() class order: class vector c("cfbfastR_data", "tbl_df", "tbl", "data.table", "data.frame"). Apply make_cfbfastR_data() final dplyr transformation, since dplyr verbs strip class. Column drift: ESPN CFBD add columns time – use subset-direction column assertions (expect_in(expected, actual)) dplyr::any_of() transient-column drops/renames. title: Get college football play-by-play data — modular EPA/WPA pipeline (v2) — cfbd_pbp_data_v2
text: year (Numeric required): Season year (e.g. 2024). season_type (Character): Season type — "regular" (default), "postseason", "", "allstar", "spring_regular", "spring_postseason". week (Numeric): Week number. team (Character): Optional team filter (e.g. "Texas"). play_type (Character): Optional play-type filter (see cfbd_play_type_df). epa_wpa (Logical): TRUE, run EPA/WPA pipeline return modeled frame; FALSE (default) return raw plays + drives + betting join. output (Character): controls modeled-output column set epa_wpa = TRUE. Ignored epa_wpa = FALSE. Defaults "default". Must one : "default" (recommended) – drops pipeline lag/lead intermediates, redundant alternates (sack_vec, turnover_indicator, kick_play, missing_yard_flag), drive-result aliases (drive_result2, drive_result_detailed_flag, lag_drive_result_detailed, lead_drive_result_detailed, lag_new_drive_pts). Keeps orig_play_type pts_scored (carry useful per-play information distinct canonical columns) per-branch WPA scratchpad (wpa_base/wpa_change etc.). ~75 columns lighter "full" loss information trivially rebuildable. "lean" – everything "default" drops, plus WPA computation scratchpad. dashboards / leaderboards / game logs. "full" – legacy behavior, drops player-name aliases. sequential modeling consumes pre-computed lag/lead shifts per-branch WPA decomposition.

code: year_vector <- 2020  week_vector <- 1:3  weekly_year_df <- expand.grid(year = year_vector, week = week_vector)  tictoc::tic()  year_split <- split(weekly_year_df, weekly_year_df$year)  for (i in 1:length(year_split)) {    i <- 1     progressr::with_progress({       year_split[[i]] <- year_split[[i]] |>          dplyr::mutate(             pbp = purrr::map2(                 .x = year,                 .y = week,                 cfbd_plays,                 season_type = "both"             )          )      Sys.sleep(1)    })  }   tictoc::toc()  year_split <- lapply(year_split, function(x) {      x |> tidyr::unnest(pbp, names_repair = "minimal")  })   all_years <- dplyr::bind_rows(year_split)  glimpse(all_years)

text: espn_cfb_award(): Get ESPN core-v2 detail record single college football award given season – name, description, history, athlete (team) won . espn_cfb_awards(): Get ESPN's college football awards season – Heisman, position player---year honors, athlete (team) won . espn_cfb_coach(): Get ESPN core-v2 detail record single college football coach – name, team coached requested season, count career-record coach-season entries ESPN file. espn_cfb_coach_record(): Get college football coach's win/loss record single season – headline summary plus every stat category ESPN publishes coach-season. espn_cfb_coaches(): Get every head coach ESPN tracks college football season, name, ESPN ids, team coached year. espn_cfb_franchise(): Get ESPN core-v2 detail record single college football franchise – location, nickname, abbreviation, color, associated venue current team, active status. espn_cfb_franchises(): Get catalog college football franchises ESPN tracks – stable program identities underpin ESPN's team resources. espn_cfb_position(): Get ESPN core-v2 detail record single college football player position – name, display name, abbreviation, leaf flag, parent position id. espn_cfb_positions(): Get catalog player positions ESPN tracks college football – position names, abbreviations, ids used throughout ESPN's athlete roster resources. espn_cfb_venue(): Get ESPN core-v2 detail record single college football venue – full name, address, playing-surface indoor flags. espn_cfb_venues(): Get catalog stadiums venues ESPN tracks college football, location, capacity-related flags, addresses. espn_cfb_clear_cache(): Clear cfbfastR ESPN catalog cache – forget memoised team position lookups next call re-fetches ESPN.

title: Clear the cfbfastR ESPN catalog cache — espn_cfb_clear_cache
text: ESPN college football game wrappers enrich output team position detail drawn two static catalogs – espn_cfb_teams() (~750 teams) espn_cfb_positions() (~74 positions). catalogs change often, internal lookups built memoised cachem + memoise, loop many games re-hit ESPN catalogs every call. espn_cfb_clear_cache() forgets memoised lookups. next wrapper call needs catalog fetch fresh copy ESPN. title: Clear the cfbfastR ESPN catalog cache — espn_cfb_clear_cache
text: Clear cfbfastR ESPN catalog cache Caching configured package load via two options(): cfbfastR.cache – cache backend. One "memory" (default; -memory cachem::cache_mem(), cleared session ends), "filesystem" (persistent -disk cachem::cache_disk() tools::R_user_dir()), "" (memoisation – every catalog fetch hits ESPN). cfbfastR.cache_duration – cache time--live seconds. Defaults 86400 (24 hours). Set options() package loaded, e.g. options(cfbfastR.cache = "filesystem"). cfbfastR.cache "", catalog helpers never memoised espn_cfb_clear_cache() -op (still returns invisibly without error).

title: ESPN College Football Game Drive Plays — espn_cfb_game_drive_plays
text: Wraps ESPN core-v2 endpoint events/{game_id}/competitions/{game_id}/drives/{drive_id}/plays. competition id always equals game id. Returns play schema competition-level espn_cfb_game_pbp() feed, partitioned single drive (typically 5-11 plays). Harvest drive_id espn_cfb_game_drives() – drive_id column lists every drive game. participants = "wide", base play schema kept intact six columns appended every participant type appears anywhere drive. column names dynamic – one set per participant type present (e.g. passer, rusher, receiver, tackler, sacked_by, pass_defender, kicker, returner). ESPN's camelCase types snake-cased (sackedBy -> sacked_by). type appended columns : {type}_player_id – scalar character, first occurrence type play (NA none). {type}_player_name – scalar character, athlete's roster-joined name (NA none unmatched). {type}_player_position – scalar character, first athlete's position abbreviation (joined ESPN position catalog; NA unmatched). {type}_player_position_name – scalar character, first athlete's position name. {type}_player_ids – list-column: character vector every athlete id type play, ESPN order. Plays none carry character(0). {type}_player_names – list-column: parallel vector roster-joined names. Participant stats[] carried wide mode – use "long" per-participant stat lines. participants = "long", frame expanded one row per play x participant participant_index, participant_athlete_id, participant_type, participant_order, roster-joined participant_athlete_name / participant_position / participant_jersey / participant_team_id, participant's stats pivoted named pstat_<statname> columns. Plays zero participants still yield one row (participant fields NA). participants_list = TRUE, single list-column named participants appended. cell tibble one row per participant play columns participant_index (1-based, ESPN order), type (snake_cased, e.g. sacked_by, pass_defender), athlete_id, athlete_name (roster-joined), order, position_id, plus one column per participant stat[] name (dplyr::bind_rows NA-fills participants whose stat sets differ). Plays participants carry empty 0-row tibble, never NULL. option independent participants composes modes – e.g. participants = "wide", participants_list = TRUE yields type-keyed {type}_player_* columns participants list-column, participants = "none", participants_list = TRUE adds list-column. participants = "long" list-column repeats per play x participant row. raw plays fetched even options active. team_participants = "wide", three columns appended every teamParticipants[] type present anywhere drive (ESPN ships offense / defense). column names dynamic – one set per type, snake-cased: {type}_team_id (scalar character, first occurrence type play), {type}_team_order (scalar integer, ESPN's display order), {type}_team_ref (scalar character, $ref URL team resource). Plays none type carry NA. team_participants_list = TRUE, single list-column named team_participants appended. cell tibble one row per team credited play columns team_participant_index (1-based, ESPN order), team_id, team_ref, order, type (e.g. offense, defense). play team participants carries empty 0-row tibble, never NULL. option independent team_participants composes – e.g. team_participants = "wide", team_participants_list = TRUE yields type-keyed {type}_team_* columns team_participants list-column, team_participants = "none" adds neither. team_detail = TRUE (default), ESPN team catalog (espn_cfb_teams()) fetched joined onto every team-id column output carries – base team_id / start_team_id / end_team_id, plus optional {type}_team_id (team_participants = "wide") {type}_player_team_id (participants = "long") columns. id column X_id friendly siblings X_name, X_abbreviation, X_location, X_display_name, X_short_display_name, X_nickname, X_color, X_alternate_color, X_logo_href, X_logo_dark_href inserted immediately (e.g. team_id -> team_name, team_abbreviation, ...; start_team_id -> start_team_name, ...). Rows whose id missing unmatched receive NA, catalog-fetch failure degrades whole set NA rather erroring wrapper. team_detail = FALSE friendly columns (catalog fetch) skipped.

title: ESPN College Football Game Drives — espn_cfb_game_drives
text: Wraps ESPN core-v2 endpoint events/{game_id}/competitions/{game_id}/drives. competition id always equals game id. Returns one row per drive (typically 18-24 drives per game). drive carries offensive team, start end period/clock/yard-line, total yards, offensive play count, drive result, scoring flag. plays_ref column $ref URL drive's plays – pass drive_id espn_cfb_game_drive_plays() fetch play--play partitioned single drive. richest drive resource ESPN exposes; site-v2 summary feed carries flattened subset. plays argument controls whether drive's plays embedded: "none" (default) – drives output returned unchanged, one row per drive, embedded plays. "list" – plays list-column appended; cell drive's plays tibble full espn_cfb_game_pbp() schema (~54 base columns plus optional participant columns). drive matched plays gets empty 0-row tibble, never NULL. "expand" – flat one-row-per-play table returned: every play full espn_cfb_game_pbp() schema, play's drive-level columns carried alongside, prefixed drive_ (e.g. drive_id, drive_result, drive_yards, drive_start_yard_line) avoid collision play's columns. espn_cfb_game_pbp() expanded form enriched drive context. participants, participants_list, team_participants, team_participants_list, position_detail arguments shape embedded plays consulted plays != "none". meaning identically named arguments espn_cfb_game_pbp() – e.g. participants = "wide" appends type-keyed {type}_player_* columns every embedded play tibble. See espn_cfb_game_pbp() full description . get plays efficiently wrapper first probes drives endpoint inline plays (items[].plays.items[]); ESPN embeds , extra request made. plays.$ref present, competition-level /plays feed fetched plays partitioned drives matching play's drive id. Per-drive plays_ref URLs never dereferenced individually. espn_cfb_unnest_plays() turns plays = "list" result flat table plays = "expand" without HTTP.

title: ESPN College Football Game Plays (Core-v2 Play-by-Play) — espn_cfb_game_pbp
text: Wraps paginated ESPN core-v2 endpoint events/{game_id}/competitions/{game_id}/plays. endpoint paginated; wrapper loops every page stacks results one frame – one row per play. play carries start end /distance/yard-line, play type, period game clock, running score, offensive team. core-v2 play feed, distinct espn_cfb_pbp(), parses site-v2 game-summary feed (optionally) computes EPA/WPA. Use wrapper want raw core-v2 play schema stable $ref-derived ids; use espn_cfb_pbp() modeled play--play. participants = "wide", base play schema kept intact six columns appended every participant type appears anywhere game. column names dynamic – one set per participant type present (e.g. passer, rusher, receiver, tackler, sacked_by, pass_defender, kicker, returner). ESPN's camelCase types snake-cased (sackedBy -> sacked_by). type appended columns : {type}_player_id – scalar character, first occurrence type play (NA none). {type}_player_name – scalar character, athlete's roster-joined name (NA none unmatched). {type}_player_position – scalar character, first athlete's position abbreviation (joined ESPN position catalog; NA unmatched). {type}_player_position_name – scalar character, first athlete's position name. {type}_player_ids – list-column: character vector every athlete id type play, ESPN order. Plays none carry character(0). {type}_player_names – list-column: parallel vector roster-joined names. Participant stats[] carried wide mode – use "long" per-participant stat lines. participants = "long", frame expanded one row per play x participant participant_index, participant_athlete_id, participant_type, participant_order, roster-joined participant_athlete_name / participant_position / participant_jersey / participant_team_id, participant's stats pivoted named pstat_<statname> columns. Plays zero participants still yield one row (participant fields NA). participants_list = TRUE, single list-column named participants appended. cell tibble one row per participant play columns participant_index (1-based, ESPN order), type (snake_cased, e.g. sacked_by, pass_defender), athlete_id, athlete_name (roster-joined), order, position_id, plus one column per participant stat[] name (dplyr::bind_rows NA-fills participants whose stat sets differ). Plays participants carry empty 0-row tibble, never NULL. option independent participants composes modes – e.g. participants = "wide", participants_list = TRUE yields type-keyed {type}_player_* columns participants list-column, participants = "none", participants_list = TRUE adds list-column. participants = "long" list-column repeats per play x participant row. raw plays fetched even options active. team_participants = "wide", three columns appended every teamParticipants[] type present anywhere game (ESPN ships offense / defense). column names dynamic – one set per type, snake-cased: {type}_team_id (scalar character, first occurrence type play), {type}_team_order (scalar integer, ESPN's display order), {type}_team_ref (scalar character, $ref URL team resource). Plays none type carry NA. team_participants_list = TRUE, single list-column named team_participants appended. cell tibble one row per team credited play columns team_participant_index (1-based, ESPN order), team_id, team_ref, order, type (e.g. offense, defense). play team participants carries empty 0-row tibble, never NULL. option independent team_participants composes – e.g. team_participants = "wide", team_participants_list = TRUE yields type-keyed {type}_team_* columns team_participants list-column, team_participants = "none" adds neither. team_detail = TRUE (default), ESPN team catalog (espn_cfb_teams()) fetched joined onto every team-id column output carries – base team_id / start_team_id / end_team_id, plus optional {type}_team_id (team_participants = "wide") {type}_player_team_id (participants = "long") columns. id column X_id friendly siblings X_name, X_abbreviation, X_location, X_display_name, X_short_display_name, X_nickname, X_color, X_alternate_color, X_logo_href, X_logo_dark_href inserted immediately (e.g. team_id -> team_name, team_abbreviation, ...; start_team_id -> start_team_name, ...). Rows whose id missing unmatched receive NA, catalog-fetch failure degrades whole set NA rather erroring wrapper. team_detail = FALSE friendly columns (catalog fetch) skipped.

title: ESPN College Football Game Play (Single Play Detail) — espn_cfb_game_play
text: game_id (Integer required): ESPN game identifier. play_id (Character required): ESPN play id (espn_cfb_game_pbp()). Supply character string – id large exact numeric. participants (Character): controls whether play's nested participants[] array (athletes credited play) attached. One : "none" (default) – single-row play frame returned unchanged; extra HTTP call made. "wide" – single row gains type-keyed {type}_player_* columns (see Details). "long" – frame expanded one row per participant (see Details). participants_list (Logical): TRUE, append single list-column named participants holding play's full participant detail – including per-participant stats[] "wide" mode drops. Defaults FALSE. independent combinable participants argument (see Details). team_participants (Character): controls whether play's nested teamParticipants[] array (team(s) credited play) attached type-keyed columns. One : "none" (default) – team-participant columns added. "wide" – single row gains type-keyed {type}_team_* columns (see Details). team_participants_list (Logical): TRUE, append single list-column named team_participants holding play's full teamParticipants[] detail nested tibble. Defaults FALSE. independent combinable team_participants argument (see Details). team_detail (Logical): TRUE (default), ESPN team catalog (espn_cfb_teams()) fetched friendly team fields joined next every team-id column output (team_id, start_team_id, end_team_id, plus optional {type}_team_id / {type}_player_team_id columns). id column X_id sibling columns X_name, X_abbreviation, X_location, X_display_name, X_short_display_name, X_nickname, X_color, X_alternate_color, X_logo_href, X_logo_dark_href inserted immediately . catalog failure degrades NA rather erroring wrapper. Set FALSE skip catalog fetch join.

title: ESPN College Football Game Play (Single Play Detail) — espn_cfb_game_play
text: Wraps ESPN core-v2 endpoint events/{game_id}/competitions/{game_id}/plays/{play_id}. competition id always equals game id. Returns single-row data frame describing one play full. Harvest play_id competition-level espn_cfb_game_pbp() feed (play_id column) espn_cfb_game_drive_plays(). Use wrapper play drill-need single play's complete object rather whole game feed. ESPN play ids 18-digit integers exceed R's exact double-precision range – pass play_id character string (e.g. "401628339101927401") precision lost. bare numeric literal silently rounded lookup 404. participants = "wide", base play schema kept intact six columns appended every participant type play. column names dynamic – one set per participant type present (e.g. passer, rusher, receiver, tackler, sacked_by, pass_defender). ESPN's camelCase types snake-cased (sackedBy -> sacked_by). type appended columns {type}_player_id (scalar character, first occurrence type play), {type}_player_name (scalar character, athlete's roster-joined name), {type}_player_position (scalar character, athlete's position abbreviation ESPN position catalog), {type}_player_position_name (scalar character, athlete's position name), {type}_player_ids (list-column: character vector every athlete id type, ESPN order; character(0) none), {type}_player_names (list-column: parallel vector roster-joined names). Participant stats[] carried wide mode – use "long" per-participant stats. participants = "long", frame expanded one row per participant participant_index, participant_athlete_id, participant_type, participant_order, roster-joined participant_athlete_name / participant_position / participant_jersey / participant_team_id, participant's stats pivoted named pstat_<statname> columns. play zero participants still yields one row (participant fields NA). participants_list = TRUE, single list-column named participants appended. one cell tibble one row per participant play columns participant_index (1-based, ESPN order), type (snake_cased, e.g. sacked_by, pass_defender), athlete_id, athlete_name (roster-joined), order, position_id, plus one column per participant stat[] name (dplyr::bind_rows NA-fills participants whose stat sets differ). play participants carries empty 0-row tibble, never NULL. option independent participants composes modes – e.g. participants = "wide", participants_list = TRUE yields type-keyed {type}_player_* columns participants list-column. participants = "long" list-column repeats per participant row. team_participants = "wide", three columns appended every teamParticipants[] type play (ESPN ships offense / defense). column names dynamic – one set per type, snake-cased: {type}_team_id (scalar character, first occurrence type play), {type}_team_order (scalar integer, ESPN's display order), {type}_team_ref (scalar character, $ref URL team resource). play none type carries NA. team_participants_list = TRUE, single list-column named team_participants appended. one cell tibble one row per team credited play columns team_participant_index (1-based, ESPN order), team_id, team_ref, order, type (e.g. offense, defense). play team participants carries empty 0-row tibble, never NULL. option independent team_participants composes – e.g. team_participants = "wide", team_participants_list = TRUE yields type-keyed {type}_team_* columns team_participants list-column, team_participants = "none" adds neither. team_detail = TRUE (default), ESPN team catalog (espn_cfb_teams()) fetched joined onto every team-id column output carries – base team_id / start_team_id / end_team_id, plus optional {type}_team_id (team_participants = "wide") {type}_player_team_id (participants = "long") columns. id column X_id friendly siblings X_name, X_abbreviation, X_location, X_display_name, X_short_display_name, X_nickname, X_color, X_alternate_color, X_logo_href, X_logo_dark_href inserted immediately (e.g. team_id -> team_name, team_abbreviation, ...; start_team_id -> start_team_name, ...). Rows whose id missing unmatched receive NA, catalog-fetch failure degrades whole set NA rather erroring wrapper. team_detail = FALSE friendly columns (catalog fetch) skipped.

title: ESPN College Football Player Season Statistics (Long Format) — espn_cfb_player_career_stats
text: data frame one row per stat:

title: ESPN College Football Player Season Statistics (Long Format) — espn_cfb_player_career_stats
text: Wraps ESPN core-v2 endpoint sports.core.api.espn.com/v2/sports/football/leagues/college-football/seasons/{year}/types/{season_type}/athletes/{athlete_id}/statistics. ESPN nests player's season stats splits -> categories[] -> stats[]; wrapper flattens tree long format – row one stat, tagged category (e.g. passing, rushing, defensive). long shape deliberate: ESPN adds retires stats whole categories across positions seasons, long frame absorbs drift without breaking column expectations. Pivot wider tidyr::pivot_wider() keyed stat_name wide table. stat carries season-total value (value) per-game value (per_game_value). athlete_detail = TRUE (default) requested athlete's ESPN record fetched human-readable name columns athlete_display_name, athlete_first_name, athlete_last_name, athlete_jersey, athlete_position, athlete_position_abbreviation appended every row. single cheap fetch – wrapper already takes one athlete_id. fetch failure degrades name columns NA rather erroring wrapper. Set athlete_detail = FALSE skip fetch reproduce prior output exactly.

title: ESPN College Football Players Index — espn_cfb_players
text: Wraps ESPN core-v2 endpoint sports.core.api.espn.com/v2/sports/football/leagues/college-football/seasons/{year}/athletes. season-scoped index contains roughly 99,500 players, returned fixed-size pages – wrapper deliberately returns id + $ref rows never dereferences individual player records, full crawl tens thousands HTTP calls. Walk index page time page, cap far single call goes max_pages. total page count season reported page_count column caller can drive pagination loop. resolve individual player full record, pass athlete_id espn_cfb_player(). athlete_detail = TRUE index enriched human-readable name columns athlete_display_name, athlete_first_name, athlete_last_name, athlete_jersey, athlete_position, athlete_position_abbreviation. bulk athlete-name catalog, resolving names costs one HTTP call per player returned – default limit = 100 100 extra requests per page. therefore defaults FALSE. per-athlete fetch failure leaves player's name columns NA rather erroring wrapper. Keep limit small (athlete_detail = FALSE) walking many pages.

Conference group ids (e.g. 4 ACC, 8 Big 12, 12 SEC, 21 Big Ten) also work. athlete_detail (Logical): TRUE, dereference quarterback append athlete_* name columns (see Details). costs one HTTP call per quarterback, defaults FALSE; setting FALSE reproduces prior output exactly.

title: ESPN College Football Total Quarterback Rating (QBR) — espn_cfb_qbr
text: Wraps ESPN core-v2 QBR endpoint seasons/{year}/types/2/groups/{group}/qbr/0. returns season--date regular-season QBR every qualified passer requested group (conference / division). group = 80 -FBS bucket sensible default; conference group ids (e.g. 4 ACC, 8 Big 12, 12 SEC, 21 Big Ten) also work. Two parameters ESPN's QBR path technically accepts deliberately exposed, neither carries data college football: .../weeks/{week}/qbr/... path returns season aggregate every week – use espn_cfb_player_stats() week-resolved passing production instead. home/away game-location split (.../qbr/1, .../qbr/2) responds 200 empty college football; total (.../qbr/0) populated. result wide – one row per quarterback – headline qbr column plus 18 component metrics ESPN derives . Players returned ESPN athlete ids (athlete_id) unless name resolution requested. athlete_detail = TRUE human-readable name columns athlete_display_name, athlete_first_name, athlete_last_name, athlete_jersey, athlete_position, athlete_position_abbreviation appended. bulk athlete-name catalog, resolving names costs one HTTP call per quarterback – roughly 130 extra requests -FBS pull. therefore defaults FALSE. per-athlete fetch failure leaves quarterback's name columns NA rather erroring wrapper. resolve names without extra calls, join athlete_id another athlete source (e.g. cfbd_team_roster()).

title: ESPN College Football Recruits — espn_cfb_recruits
text: Wraps ESPN core-v2 endpoint sports.core.api.espn.com/v2/sports/football/leagues/college-football/seasons/{year}/recruits. season index $ref-paginated large (roughly 3,700-4,900 recruits per class), dereferencing every recruit thousands HTTP calls. ESPN exposes pre-expanded recruiting endpoint – site.web.api.espn.com recruiting paths 404 – wrapper caps walk max_results recruits (default 100). Raise max_results (e.g. several hundred higher) pull class, cost one extra HTTP call per recruit. index returned ESPN athlete-name (alphabetical) order, ranking order, sort query parameter ignored upstream. default max_results = 100 therefore returns alphabetically-first 100 recruits, top-100 ranked recruits. rank class, pull larger slice sort result overall_rank (lower better); note ESPN publishes overall_rank highly-rated portion class, recruits carry NA . position_rank, state_rank, region_rank populated widely. grade ESPN's 0-100 recruit grade (0 / gradeDisplayValue = "NR" means rated). committed_team_id / committed_team_ref resolved recruit's schools array matching school whose commitment status equals recruit's top-level status (e.g. Signed); recruits still uncommitted fetch time leave columns NA.

title: ESPN College Football Standings (Long Format) — espn_cfb_standings
text: year (Integer required): Season, 4 digit format (YYYY). group_id (Integer default 90): ESPN group id. 90 = NCAA Division (D-teams). Conference group ids also work. season_type (Integer default 2): ESPN season type id. 2 = regular season. team_detail (Logical): TRUE (default), fetch ESPN team catalog join friendly team fields next team_id column (see Details). Set FALSE skip catalog fetch join.

title: ESPN College Football Standings (Long Format) — espn_cfb_standings
text: data frame one row per team-record-statistic:

title: ESPN College Football Standings (Long Format) — espn_cfb_standings
text: Wraps ESPN core-v2 endpoint sports.core.api.espn.com/v2/sports/football/leagues/college-football/seasons/{year}/types/{season_type}/groups/{group_id}/standings. standings resource nests three levels deep – team -> record split -> statistic – wrapper returns long format: one row per (team x record split x statistic). long shape absorbs ESPN's habit adding standings stats across seasons. Pivot wider keyed stat_name (within record_type) wide table wanted. group_id = 90 (NCAA Division ) sensible default yields every D-team one call. Conference-level group_ids – enumerate espn_cfb_groups() – restrict table conference. team_detail = TRUE (default) ESPN team catalog (espn_cfb_teams()) fetched friendly team fields joined next team_id column – team_name, team_abbreviation, team_location, team_display_name, team_short_display_name, team_nickname, team_color, team_alternate_color, team_logo_href, team_logo_dark_href, inserted immediately team_id. catalog failure degrades NA rather erroring wrapper. Set team_detail = FALSE skip catalog fetch join.

what: ESPN College Football Team Endpoint Overview — espn_cfb_team
title: ESPN College Football Team Endpoint Overview — espn_cfb_team
text: espn_cfb_team(): Get ESPN's detailed record single college football team given season – identifiers, branding, conference grouping, home venue. espn_cfb_teams(): Get full ESPN directory college football teams – one row per team identifiers, branding, conference grouping, logo URLs. espn_cfb_team_ats(): Get college football team's --spread (ATS) records season – 6-7 betting split rows ESPN tracks (overall, favorite, underdog, home, away, ...). espn_cfb_team_awards(): Get awards won college football team's players season – one row per (award x winning athlete). espn_cfb_team_coaches(): Get coaches associated college football team season – one row per coach, name, birth detail, experience. espn_cfb_team_events(): Get college football team's full season event log – every game (regular season postseason) ESPN lists team-season. espn_cfb_team_leaders(): Get college football team's season statistical leaders – top athletes ESPN leader category (passing, rushing, receiving, tackles, ...). espn_cfb_team_powerindex(): Get ESPN's College Football Power Index (FPI) detail single team-season – full set predictive metrics efficiency components ESPN attaches one team. espn_cfb_team_ranks(): Get college football team's poll-rank history season – one row per poll (AP, Coaches, CFP Committee, ...) team appeared . espn_cfb_team_record(): Get college football team's season records – overall, home, away, conference splits – full set summary stats ESPN attaches . espn_cfb_team_roster(): Get season roster single college football team – one row per athlete biographical detail, position, jersey number, class/experience. espn_cfb_team_schedule(): Get single college football team's full-season schedule – one row per game opponent, venue, broadcast, score, result. espn_cfb_team_stats(): Get ESPN college football team season statistics – wide tibble team identifiers per-category statistical totals. title: Update or create a cfbfastR play-by-play database — update_cfb_db
text: function creates updates data table name tblname within SQLite database (drivers via db_connection) located dbdir named dbname. data table combines play play data every available game back 2014 season adds recent completed games soon available cfbfastR. argument force_rebuild hybrid type. can rebuild play play data table either whole cfbfastR era (force_rebuild = TRUE) just specified seasons (e.g. force_rebuild = c(2019, 2020)). Please note following behavior: force_rebuild = TRUE : data table name tblname removed completely rebuilt scratch. helpful new columns added -Season. force_rebuild = c(2019, 2020) : data table name tblname preserved rows 2019 2020 seasons deleted re-added. intended used ongoing seasons ESPN's data provider can make changes underlying data week. parameter db_connection intended advanced users want use DBI drivers, MariaDB, Postgres odbc. Please note arguments dbdir dbname dropped case db_connection provided argument tblname still used write data table database.

title: Get Yahoo Sports college football player season stats (modern) — yahoo_cfb_player_season_stats
text: Flattens shangrila leagueStatsIndividual response (stat groups one call) one wide tibble one row per player. NCAAF data available 2013-present.

title: Get Yahoo Sports college football player season stats (modern) — yahoo_cfb_player_season_stats
code: yahoo_cfb_player_season_stats(   season = most_recent_cfb_season(),   league_structure = "ncaaf.struct.div.1",   count = 200,   qualified = FALSE )

title: Get Yahoo Sports college football player season stats (modern) — yahoo_cfb_player_season_stats
text: season (integer): Season year (e.g. 2024). Defaults most_recent_cfb_season(). league_structure (character): Division filter. Defaults "ncaaf.struct.div.1" (FBS). count (integer): Max players. Defaults 200. qualified (logical): Restrict qualified leaders. Defaults FALSE.

title: Get Yahoo Sports college football player season stats (modern) — yahoo_cfb_player_season_stats
text: cfbfastR-tagged tibble one row per player. Core columns: player_id: character.: Yahoo player id (ncaaf.p.*). display_name: character.: Player name. team: character.: Team display name. team_abbreviation: character.: Team abbreviation. season: integer.: Season echoed back. Remaining columns one per statId (e.g. passing_yards, rushing_yards, receptions, ...), value displayed (character). Column set grows time.

Verified live 2025 season. fox_cfb_pbp() — game play--play (quarters → drives → plays), one row per play. fox_cfb_boxscore() — per-team player stat tables, tidy long (one row per player-stat). fox_cfb_odds() — matchup six-pack (spread / -win / total) per team. fox_cfb_team_roster() — roster position group, one row per player. fox_cfb_team_stats() — team stat leaders category. fox_cfb_team_gamelog() — per-game team stats, tidy long (game × category × stat), game keyed Fox event id. fox_cfb_standings() — team’s conference standings table. fox_cfb_league_leaders() — statistical leaderboards category (stats-con).

title: cfbfastR v2.3.0
text: httr -> httr2 migration. cfbfastR’s HTTP layer now uses modern httr2 package (>= 1.0.0) instead legacy httr. End users running existing wrapper calls (cfbd_*, espn_cfb_*) see behavioural change – migration internal. Custom code calls get_req() check_status() directly must update httr::content(res, = "text") httr2::resp_body_string(res) httr::status_code(res) httr2::resp_status(res). Proxy support. get_req() now resolves proxy order: explicit proxy argument -> getOption("cfbfastR.proxy") -> http_proxy / https_proxy env vars. proxy value accepts either URL string named list url / port / username / password / auth authenticated proxies. Dependency footprint trimmed. lubridate, progressr, memoise, cachem, magrittr moved Imports (21 -> 16). lubridate gone entirely – two ymd_hm() |> with_tz() calls espn_cfb_schedule.R now base-R .POSIXct(format = "%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M", tz = "UTC") + attr(., "tzone"). progressr, memoise, cachem moved Suggests helpers degrade gracefully missing: load_cfb_pbp() / cfbd_pbp_data() / pbp_epa_wpa_engine() run without progress bar progressr absent; ESPN catalog wrappers run uncached memoise / cachem absent (espn_cfb_clear_cache() becomes -op). Drops Imports count >20 R CMD check NOTE threshold. Native pipe migration. 1,419 %>% chains R/, plus 137 across vignettes/ tests/, converted base-R native pipe |>. magrittr longer Imports; downstream consumers load cfbfastR purely functions don’t get %>% re-exported anymore. User-visible impact minimal – public API unchanged dplyr (Imports) still re-exports %>% users want keep writing . Two non-mechanical fixes needed sweep: three |> [[("url") chains cfbd_betting.R cfbd_coaches.R (rejected RHS R 4.1’s |>) became |> purrr::pluck("url"); seven |> tibble::tibble(col = .data$.) constructs magrittr quirk silently duplicated LHS . named column – rewritten tibble::tibble(col = <lhs>), drops redundant . column. Test-time CFBD throttle. new tests/testthat/setup-cfbd-throttle.R adds 1-second sleep every CFBD request made devtools::test() / R CMD check. works monkey-patching cfbfastR:::get_req() duration test session (restored via withr::defer(., teardown_env())) – package code unchanged, interactive production calls pay penalty. Tunable via options(cfbfastR.test_request_delay = N) (default 1; set 0 unthrottled local runs). Resolves cascading HTTP 429 skip--empty results turning otherwise-green test runs “green, mostly skipped.” withr joins Suggests declare test-side dependency cleanly (already transitive dep testthat).
